issue: declare -A (bash 4+) crashes on macOS bash 3.2; called by rad-deliver/rad-review. Verified real; FIXED (newline-delimited scope list). Pre-existing on main.
RAD_BRANCH_PREFIX embedded in =~ regex unescaped. FIXED with literal prefix test.
Claimed sed-escape breaks branch validation; adversarially verified FALSE — works for default and normal prefixes. No change.
GitLab label list leading-comma + unquoted label word-splitting. Pre-existing in untouched open_gitlab(); out of scope for this PR.
collect_logs find|xargs ls -t word-splits/space-bug. Pre-existing in untouched function; out of scope.
No GitHub zero-label test case (the previously-buggy empty-array branch). FIXED: added case 5.
Negative assertions could false-green if a stub never wrote its argv file. FIXED: require_called guard.

tasks_done/failed could be empty (unreadable file) → empty numeric operand. FIXED with ${var:-0}; verified [[ "" -gt 0 ]] does not actually crash. Reviewer's suggested || echo 0 rejected (regresses #3).
t3 fixture lacked .agents/plans/. FIXED (added + comment); plans path covered elsewhere.
t4 didn't exercise the #4 placeholder-strip branch. FIXED: fixture now includes the placeholder line + asserts it is filtered.
ensure_deliver_label fallback message ambiguous. FIXED: clearer wording referencing step 2.

Doom-loop check fires before resolveOutcome; fingerprint() excludes outcome, so a success with empty categories/summary hashes equal to a prior empty-fingerprint failure, aborting on a genuine success.
feature parameter used unsanitised in path.join() and as a shell arg; a slug containing '../..' escapes repoRoot. No format validation in append/history/plan/phase/gate.
resolvePath escape hatch: any name with '/' or '.' is joined onto repoRoot with no bounds check; name='../../../etc/passwd' resolves outside repoRoot. feature also unsanitised.

withTempRepo is synchronous but two gate tests pass async callbacks; finally deletes the temp dir before the async body runs, so gate I/O hits a deleted directory — structurally broken, false confidence.
resolveOutcome hardcoded to phase 'implement'; the 'to:' field is never consumed, so matrix.yaml's 'verify' phase rows are unreachable, contradicting the matrix comment.
append() validates event.feature but not event.type or event.actor; a missing type persists and corrupts the phase fold irreversibly; a missing actor bypasses downstream role checks.
Escape hatch for names with '/' or '.' silently discards feature; name='plan.md' writes to <repoRoot>/plan.md with no feature namespace, clobbering plans. Undocumented.
No test for the budget-exhaustion path (MAX_ATTEMPTS distinct-fingerprint failures) or the 'surface' matrix action (fail-timeout) — distinct terminal paths with separate side-effects.
No test for null plan or empty waves; spine silently skips the loop and opens a PR — no assertion pins whether that is the intended contract.
MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 but the comment says 'Case uses two cycles' — value/comment disagree; constant is not injectable for tests.
Lazy-import comment implies js-yaml is optional, but spine.js imports matrix.js at top level which loads js-yaml eagerly — may mislead about the harness-level dep.
Approval test asserts deepEqual on { recordedBy: undefined } — an implementation-detail assertion that would break on a valid tightening of reduce() with no behavioral regression.

parseWaveResult defaults an unrecognized task status to 'complete'; a typo'd/novel status makes resultToOutcome return 'success' and the wave advances on a blocked task (silent failure masking). Safe default should be a non-passing status.

resultToOutcome maps blocked_spec/blocked_intent to fail-tests (matrix action: revision/retry) but the wave taxonomy says those are non-retryable escalations; mapping them to fail-scope (action: abort) escalates instead of wasting bounded retries. Achievable with existing outcomes (no matrix change).

SDK is_error summary is passed to new Error() before sanitizeErrorMessage; the catch sanitizes before logging so exposure is defense-in-depth, but sanitizing at construction makes the no-leak invariant hold regardless of SDK behavior.

spawnOnce accumulates stdout/stderr with no size cap; a misbehaving agent emitting large output exhausts memory before the wall-clock timeout fires. Add a soft cap that kills the child and returns fail-protocol.

Timeout-vs-spawn-error discriminator parses the 'timed out' substring rather than a sentinel property set by withTimeout; a spawn-level ETIMEDOUT could be misrouted to fail-timeout. Use err._isRadTimeout.
deliverCommand top-level catch writes err.message to stderr without sanitizeErrorMessage; a deep spine error could surface a credential fragment.
sanitizeErrorMessage 40-char catch-all redacts Git SHAs and long paths, harming debuggability (pre-existing, relocated from runwave.js).
Module comment references runwave.js which no longer exists; should reference adapters/agent/sdk.js.
part.replace('{prompt}', prompt) is non-global; only the first {prompt} token per argument is substituted.
No test covers a non-zero exit on the reprompt (second) invocation; only the first-call non-zero path is exercised.

Per-wave gate demotion fingerprinted the model's variable result text, so a gate that fails identically while the model rewords its output never trips the doom-loop and burns the whole attempt budget. FIXED: fingerprint stable gate-derived fields.
Malformed wave-complete test did not assert completed.size, so removing the data guard would not be caught. FIXED: asserts size===1 against no-data/no-wave/string-id events.
Already-complete resume test used an untracked sh mock; resume-verify running when it shouldn't would not be caught. FIXED: tracking sh asserts check-tests.sh never runs when all waves complete.
resumeFrom did not type-check data.wave; a string id would be added and never match the numeric wave.n (silent mis-skip). FIXED: typeof === 'number' guard.

deliver-started is appended before resumeFrom reads history, so each crash-resume accumulates an extra deliver-started event. DEFERRED: harmless (reduce/phaseOf tolerate it); revisit if diagnostics need a run count.
sh is typed synchronous but not enforced; an async sh injection would make status checks evaluate on a Promise (never 0). DEFERRED: add a runtime guard or async-tolerant contract later.
